correctness.rationale: For finite noncommutative nilpotent semigroups with zero, the full power semiring includes all subsets (also empty) in the constant-free binary signature. The nilpotent power filtration makes indices <=4 at order<=4; index two is commutative and noncommutative index-four order-five cases have nonzero pure cube, giving finite basis by the explicitly credited published sufficient condition. At order five, index-three and zero squares reduce to either three generators and one nonzero product value (loopless 3-vertex digraph support) or exactly two generators with two distinct mixed-product values. I independently enumerated all 63 nonempty labeled loopless digraphs into 15 isomorphism types, computed induced retract cores, their categorical squares and complete domination-removal searches: 12 classes are noncommutative, of which eight fail finite duality, with canonical six-bit strings 000110,000111,001111,010101,011001,011011,011110,011111; the other four have finite duality. The bidirected two-generator/two-output type adds one further nonfinite-duality class. The infinite nonfinite-equational-basis conclusion depends essentially on the published finite-duality/full-power-semiring equivalence; the finite checker is not a substitute. The structural all-types reduction, source verify.py and acyclic-path unbounded odd-cycle obstruction were read and checked. Hence the sharp minimum size five and nine noncommutative isomorphism classes follow under stated external theorems.

The result is useful to finite-semigroup databases and as concrete benchmark cases for the existing finite-duality criterion; no new general criterion is falsely claimed.
